Bullion declined as much as 3.7% to $3,426.77 an ounce. A rout in gold has gathered pace recently, with the metal plunging nearly 9% last week, on track for a third straight monthly decline of more than 6%. Bloomberg's Mike McGlone joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Michael Burry Is More Long Than Short After Dumping Nasdaq Puts
general.summary: The selloff in technology stocks has left investor Michael Burry, who became famous for betting against the US mortgage market in 2008, with more long equity positions than short ones after unloading his put options on the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index.

general.title: US Army Detonates Explosives Cache in Middletown, Iowa
general.summary: The US Army blew up five tons of hazardous materials stored at a facility in Iowa, with early indications suggesting planners had averted the worst-case scenario of a massive cloud of toxic lead. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: El Salvador Finally Reaps Economic Gains From Gang Crackdown
general.summary: El Salvador’s economic fortunes are finally starting to match its dramatic improvement in security.

general.title: Fed, AI Fears Rattle Markets
general.summary: Stocks slide as investors question whether the AI boom can deliver profits soon enough. Bloomberg’ Macro Strategist Michael Ball and Ira Jersey, Chief US Rates Strategist at Bloomberg Intelligence discuss the market’s selloff, Treasury demand, oil-price risks, and what the Fed’s next moves could mean for yields. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Bank of England Rate-Setters Leave December Hike on the Table
general.summary: Three Bank of England policymakers said they cannot ignore the threat to inflation from persistently high energy prices, leaving the door open to a further interest-rate hike next month.

general.title: Anthropic’s Post-IPO Struggles Contrast With SpaceX’s Early Days
general.summary: Anthropic PBC is experiencing a rougher initiation to public markets than SpaceX, and a host of market and technical factors threaten to weigh down its stock performance before the Claude developer reports for the first time as a public company early next year.

general.title: Trump’s New Tariffs: How Are Import Taxes Affecting the Economy?
general.summary: In the first half of his second term as US president, Donald Trump has made tariffs central to his economic policy. In midterm elections in early November, in which his Republican Party lost control of both chambers of Congress to the Democrats, exit polls captured deep voter dissatisfaction with tariffs. The levies have been shown to raise the prices consumers pay for imported goods. Trump is moving to expand them nonetheless.

general.title: Russian Refinery Runs Drop to Lowest in Decades, Rystad Says
general.summary: Russia’s oil processing rates have plunged to the lowest in more than two decades as Ukraine continues to strike refineries, according to Rystad Energy, heaping pressure on the country’s domestic fuel supplies.

general.title: Power On: What to Make of Cook’s Relationship with Trump
general.summary: A 70-year-old Apple fan who still owns his original iPhone wrote in to ask: Why is Tim Cook making so many concessions to Donald Trump—and will John Ternus change things? On the Power On podcast, Mark Gurman breaks down the tension inside Apple over Tim Cook’s political playbook. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Nasdaq 100 Enters Bear Market Territory as AI Angst Fuels Losses
general.summary: The Nasdaq 100 Index plunged for a second day, sending it careening into bear-market territory as traders dumped technology shares, with worries around AI dominating sentiment on Wall Street. Bloomberg US Equities Team Lead, Elena Popina discusses AI sentiment and the ongoing rout in tech shares. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Russia October Inflation Hits One-Year High as War Escalates
general.summary: Russian inflation accelerated to the fastest pace in a year in October as persistent drone strikes deep inside the country reduced production capacity.

general.title: Deere Down on Earnings; Dell Lower Despite Server Sales | Stock Movers
general.summary: On this episode of Stock Movers: - Deere (DE) shares are lower as it reports earnings this morning, with the focus of investors being on the farm economy and whether it will emerge from a prolonged slump that's pressured sales of tractors and other agricultural equipment. Deere reported earnings per share for the fourth quarter that missed the average analyst estimate. - Dell Technologies (DELL) is lower this morning even after it boosted its fiscal year revenue sales outlook

general.title: Billions in Data Center Deals Grind to Halt After AI Chip Curbs
general.summary: Lenders have hit the brakes on billions of dollars in loans tied to Chinese firms ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent, as new US curbs on chip access threaten to upend Asia’s burgeoning AI debt financing market.

general.title: Stocks Swoon as AI Fears Spur Rush to Treasuries
general.summary: The rout in tech shares is showing no sign of letting up as questions about the artificial-intelligence outlook pile up, with traders turning to bonds despite elevated inflation data. Seema Shah, Chief Global Strategist at Principal Asset Management, gives her equity outlook for the rest of 2026 as traders continue to dump technology shares. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Underlying AI Demand 'Much Bigger' than Market Pricing In, Says Ives
general.summary: The Nasdaq 100 Index plunged for a second day, sending it careening into bear-market territory as traders dumped technology shares, with worries around AI dominating sentiment on Wall Street. Dan Ives, Partner at Yorkville Ives & Co, discusses the continued pullback in tech and what 2027 will bring to the world of AI investment. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: ECB in No Rush to Increase Banks’ Minimum Reserves After Debate
general.summary: European Central Bank officials are unlikely to make any imminent change in the amount of money euro-zone banks must hold at the institution even if several are leaning toward an increase, people familiar with the matter said.

general.title: JPMorgan Backs Drone Engine Maker’s Muni Sale in Wisconsin
general.summary: A drone engine manufacturer is making its debut in the US municipal bond market with a familiar name standing behind the debt: JPMorgan Chase & Co.

general.title: New US Home Sales Reach Highest This Year, Topping Forecasts
general.summary: New-home sales in the US unexpectedly climbed last month to the highest level this year as builders leaned heavily on costly sales incentives to offset the spike in mortgage rates.

general.title: Trump open to pardoning Jensen Huang if needed: NY Post
general.summary: Trump said he would be willing to pardon Jensen Huang if needed and argued that the Nvidia CEO should not have to invoke the Fifth Amendment before Congress.

general.title: México eleva presión fiscal y laboral sobre Rappi y Uber
general.summary: Nuevas medidas fiscales amenazan con elevar aún más los costos de las plataformas de entrega en el país.

general.title: What the PCE Data Means for Fed Policy
general.summary: The Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of underlying inflation, the personal consumption expenditures price index excluding food and energy, rose 0.3%. From a year earlier, core PCE was up 3.3%, the most since 2023 — keeping Fed policymakers on track for an interest-rate hike next month. Bloomberg Intelligence's Ira Jersey has the details. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Embraer Shares Sink as US Threatens Brazil Aircraft Tariff
general.summary: Embraer SA shares fell the most in more than six months after the US proposed a 10% tariff on aircraft from Brazil, threatening the planemaker’s business in one of its most important markets.

general.title: Stocks Selloff Hits Unlikely Market, Sinking Carry Trade
general.summary: One of Wall Street’s most reliable wagers of 2026 is starting to lose its surefire status.

general.title: BC Partners Buys GSE Agency With Golfer DeChambeau on List
general.summary: BC Partners’ credit arm has agreed to buy a majority stake in GSE Worldwide, a sports marketing agency which represents athletes such as golf celebrity Bryson DeChambeau and former NFL and MLB star Bo Jackson.

general.title: Uber, Rappi Face Fresh Tax Squeeze After Mexico Gig-Labor Reform
general.summary: New tax measures are adding to the cost pressures that Rappi and Uber face in Mexico, where a sweeping labor reform and mounting regulatory charges have made it one of the costliest Latin American markets for delivery apps.

general.title: US Consumers Press Pause After Strong Spending Last Quarter
general.summary: US consumer spending stalled in October after surging earlier in the year, suggesting households took a breather heading into the holiday season.

general.title: Trump’s meddling in Huang scandal reignites voter angst over tech’s outsized political power
general.summary: Nvidia’s decision to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang after pressure from Trump is intensifying bipartisan scrutiny of tech companies' ties to the administration.
